thread:
sarah: Running an nsys capture on a low-latency KV-cache run and a bunch of CUDA kernels show up with no stack frames / no line info in the timeline. only kernel names and generic addresses. anyone seen this?

sarah: command i ran: `nsys profile --output kv-nsys --sample=none --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=nvtx:trace --nvtx-threads=1 --nvtx-plain-ids=true python run_kvcache.py`

sarah: attached the .qdrep (uploaded to /tmp) — but timeline is basically blank for our runtime functions, hard to tell which kernel maps to which call site.

miguel: are the binaries in the container built with debug info? missing `-g` or `-fno-omit-frame-pointer` will make line info vanish. also check if we stripped the runtime.

kevin: also CUPTI mismatch can do this — if CUPTI/nvtx hooks are from a different CUDA toolkit than the driver+runtime you're profiling, symbolization can fail. what CUDA version did you use inside the container vs host driver?

sarah: container CUDA 12.2, host driver 12.1 (we mount host driver libs). could that be it?

miguel: yep. CUPTI maintains unwind/symbolization helpers that expect certain offsets. Mismatch -> no frame unwinding. try running `nvcc --version` in container and `nvidia-smi` on host and confirm.

rachel: small checklist we usually run:
- ensure build flags: `-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fno-optimize-sibling-calls` for C++ runtime code you want lines for
- if using python bindings (pybind11), compile extension with `-g` too
- confirm the runtime binary in the container matches the one used when building (no mount/overlay mismatch)
- mount `/usr/lib/debug` or ship debug packages into the container if you want full symbols

perf-bot: quick tip — nvtx ranges help: add NVTX around high-level calls so even if stack is missing, you see named blocks.

kevin: another oddness: we had container images where `glibc` version differences caused addr2line to fail to find lines because debuginfo path resolution changed. highly unlikely but happened to us with a CUDA 11 -> 12 shuffle.

sarah: ok i'm rebuilding with `-g` and bumping compile flags. but is there a way to force nsys to show raw addresses so i can addr2line myself?

miguel: yes use `nsys export --output <report> --format sqlite` or use `nsys stats -r` to get raw addresses. also `cuobjdump --dump-sass` on the cubin can help map kernels. if you have the host binary, run `addr2line -e /path/to/binary 0xADDR` to get file:line.

sarah: tried `nsys export` — still no function names for our runtime frames, only `libc`/`ld` entries.

rachel: can you paste sample stack from the qdrep? (just the top few frames)

sarah: pasted below (copied from timeline view):
```
CUcontext_ KernelLaunch
<unknown>+0x1f2
<unknown>+0x44d
libc.so.6+0x7a1b
```

miguel: that `unknown` pattern is classic when debug symbols are missing or the binary loaded at different base address. did you do ASLR?

kevin: also check the container's /proc/<pid>/maps for the mapping base; sometimes our packaging strips symbol tables but the file exists at a different path in the mounted image. container overlay bug we hit last sprint.

sarah: re-built runtime with `-g` and re-ran. timeline is better but still missing lines for a couple of small helper functions that call kernels — stack frame for those still shows `<no-symbol>`

miguel: could be inlined or optimized away. try `-O1` or disable inlining for those files (`noinline` attribute) to preserve frames. also `-funwind-tables` / `-fasynchronous-unwind-tables` helps with unwinding in optimized builds.

sarah: good call. adding `-fno-inline` to the hotpath functions made them appear. thanks.

rachel: FYI if you're using LTO, that can also confuse addr2line since code layout changes. ensure the build you profile is the exact same build you run `addr2line` against.

sarah: one more weird thing — KV cache kernel selection code is choosing small-block kernels and i can't correlate why. the perftimeline doesn't show which kernel call site selected the kernel (no source lines). any tips to make the mapping explicit?

kevin: NVTX + more granular NVTX ranges around the kernel selection logic helps. also add unique NVTX colors/strings when you choose a kernel variant, e.g., `nvtxRangePushA("kvcache::select_kernel: small_block_v2")`. then in the timeline the kernel shows up inside that range.

miguel: and consider adding a host-side trace event with a monotonic id that you pass as kernel arg (one int). Then dump kernel metadata and cross-ref id -> source. slightly invasive but rock-solid.

sarah: i tried NVTX tags but some kernels still look unlabeled because we call kernels from a helper inlined by compiler. NVTX is before the call but inlining collapses it.

rachel: wrap NVTX in a noinline function or mark NVTX callsite with `asm volatile ("" ::: "memory")` to prevent reordering/inlining around it. also keep NVTX strings static so they survive symbol stripping.

sarah: re-ran with noinline NVTX wrapper + `-g` + matching CUPTI version. the timeline now shows our helper frames and the kernel variant mapping. found the bug — batching heuristic was miscomputing slot count under edge case mask which caused wrong kernel pick.

miguel: nice! did you repro locally on CI too? any perf regression after changing flags?

sarah: fixed heuristic and rebench. latency improved ~6% p99 on small sequences. rebuilds with `-g` increased binary size but runtime perf unchanged. will remove `-g` in release builds but keep `-fasynchronous-unwind-tables` and `noinline` for NVTX glue to help future traces.

kevin: great — we should add a small doc snippet in eng-runtime about reproducible profiling: container CHECKLIST, CUPTI version matrix, nvtx best practices, and the sample nsys command. i can draft.

rachel: also add a note about `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda` vs `--trace=cuda` differences for frame capture. `nvtx` helps group and keep ranges even when CUPTI can't fully unwind.

sarah: thanks all. i'll drop the qdrep in the perf bucket and mark this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
